- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next period.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior period), model often overshoots; apply a 3–7 day lag correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33 or 0.00), model frequently fails to adjust downward; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 2–5 days.
- In low-sentiment (≤0.33) periods, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–4% to account for mean reversion toward historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; smooth forecast using 5-day moving average of prior 10-day trend.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often misjudges direction; use sentiment-weighted average of 3-day high/low to anchor forecast.
